beats.narration: Your phone may be keeping a map of the places you go. Including this one.
beats.visual: Dark bedroom at night, phone on a nightstand. Screen snaps on: an unnamed city map at night; a red trail draws itself pin by pin; the last pin pulses. On-screen label: 'Illustration'.

beats.narration: On iPhone, with Significant Locations and Routes on, it keeps track of where you've recently been, how often, when, and your routes.
beats.visual: Wide moonlit bedroom, slow dolly toward the nightstand; cut to a macro of the phone as a list of visited places with times fills in (generic place names, no real person's data, not styled as iPhone Settings). On-screen label: 'Illustration'.

beats.narration: On Android, Google Maps Timeline is off until you turn it on. Then it saves your visits and routes to your phone, even with Google apps closed.
beats.visual: Night aerial over an unnamed city (street layout from OpenStreetMap, buildings modelled, no place names). The city is quiet at first; then a red line draws one made-up day's route along the streets, a light marks each stop as it is reached, and the camera rises to show the whole route. No phone UI, no Google branding. On-screen labels: 'Illustration' and the map-data credit.
onScreenText: Android: Google Maps Timeline (off by default)

beats.narration: On iPhone, Apple says it can't read it. Google keeps it on your phone, unless you back it up.
beats.visual: Slow push down into the glowing map; trails like handwriting across the city. On-screen label: 'Illustration'.
Clean on-screen steps over the dimmed nightstand, each line appearing in turn.
onScreenText: iPhone: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services
Android: Google Maps > profile picture or initial

beats.narration: You can set Google Maps to auto-delete it after three, eighteen or thirty-six months. Or never: then it's kept until you delete it. If it's on, it's on your phone right now. Go check.
beats.visual: The map zooms out: one night's trail becomes a dense glowing web over the whole city (on-screen label 'Illustration'); heartbeat accelerates then stops; silence; the auto-delete card appears, then 'Off = kept until you delete it'; the screen switches off and its black glass reflects the bedroom; one low hit; cut to black.
onScreenText: Timeline auto-delete: 3, 18 or 36 months, or off
Off = kept until you delete it

caption:
Your phone may keep a map of where you go. Here is where each setting lives.
LU-TECH-003

iPhone: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > Significant Locations & Routes.
Android: Google Maps > profile picture or initial > Your Timeline.

Sources:
- Apple, "Location Services & Privacy", apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/location-services
- Apple Personal Safety User Guide, "Manage Location Services settings", support.apple.com
- Google Maps Help, "Manage your Google Maps Timeline" (Android and iPhone), support.google.com/maps/answer/6258979
Limits: Google says Timeline is off by default and only on if you opt in. Apple's pages cited here don't say whether Significant Locations & Routes is on by default, show how to view it only on a Mac, and don't say whether turning it off clears what's saved. On Google Maps, turning Timeline off isn't the same as deleting it (Turn off and delete activity); optional backups are encrypted copies on Google's servers; other Google settings such as Web & App Activity can also save location info. Menu names can differ by version and language. Apple and Google describe their own encryption; this video does not test it. Map visuals are illustrations; map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
